top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
top_sast_rules.description: Invoking user-controlled methods on certain objects can lead to remote code execution.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement secure coding practices specific to this vulnerability type. Review the query logic for detailed requirements.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
top_sast_rules.description: Using externally controlled strings in a command line may allow a malicious user to change the meaning of the command.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement secure coding practices specific to CWE-088. Review OWASP guidelines and CWE documentation for detailed mitigation strategies.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')
top_sast_rules.description: Externally influenced data changes the syntax or meaning of a command sent to a downstream command interpreter.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-77 command-injection command-construction shell exec spawn process subprocess child_process os.system popen argument-delimiter metacharacter
top_sast_rules.remediation: Keep external data separate from command syntax and use safe argument APIs.

top_sast_rules.description: Deserializing user-controlled data may allow attackers to execute arbitrary code.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Identify deserialization operations on untrusted data without proper validation
top_sast_rules.remediation: Use safe serialization formats like JSON. If complex deserialization is needed, implement strict validation and type checking.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')
top_sast_rules.description: Building an XPath expression from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious code by the user.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement path validation using canonical paths. Reject paths containing '../' or similar traversal sequences.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
top_sast_rules.description: Recursively merging a user-controlled object into another object can allow an attacker to modify the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement proper output encoding based on context (HTML, JavaScript, CSS, URL). Use Content Security Policy and validate input.

top_sast_rules.description: Using cookies without CSRF protection may allow malicious websites to submit requests on behalf of the user.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Find state-changing operations that lack CSRF protection mechanisms
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement CSRF tokens for all state-changing operations. Use SameSite cookie attributes and validate the Origin/Referer headers.
